tasks.severity_note: Go-live blocker: reproduced WITHOUT a sanitizer. Remote denial of service (process death) reachable from one web_open call.
tasks.title: HTML parse on a cooperative task stack exhausts the stack and kills the process
tasks.evidence_before: Without any sanitizer: `swift test --filter AUDITDiagnosticsTests/testD_deepNestingThresholdWithoutASan` survives depth 1000 (clean malformedResponse) and DIES at depth 5000 with signal 10 (SIGBUS); `testE_deepNestingThroughHTMLExtraction` dies at depth 20000. With ASan the same failure appears at much lower depths and as a BUS in _platform_memset on a cooperative task (Task 3), which is how it was first found: `swift test --sanitize=address --filter ProviderContractTests/testDuckDuckGoTaxonomy` => signal 6. Attribution matrix: ScraperSupport.parse synchronously on the junk body = ok; DDG provider async on the same body = crash; DDG provider async on well-formed empty HTML = ok; TSan clean.
tasks.fix_summary: (1) MarkupDepth.containsMarkup rejects a body with no markup at all before parsing (ScraperSupport throws malformedResponse(provider)); scoped to the scrapers, because the web_open extractor must keep accepting plain text, JSON and YAML. (2) MarkupDepth.exceedsLimit counts element nesting iteratively on the raw bytes with an early exit and a cap of 512 (maximumNesting): comments, declarations, void elements, self-closing tags and raw-text element content (script/style/...) open no level, a '>' in a quoted attribute does not end a tag, a stray '<' is text. Exceeding it throws the new SearchError.markupDepthExceeded(limit), category .malformedResponse. (3) LargeStackParse.run executes the recursive part of ScraperSupport.parse and HTMLExtractor.extract on a dedicated 8 MiB-stack thread, synchronously, publishing the outcome through a Sendable OSAllocatedUnfairLock (no @unchecked Sendable, no unsynchronised shared state, deadlock-free because the parse thread does no Swift concurrency work). (4) Tests/WebSearchCoreTests/MarkupDepthTests.swift: 19 tests, including the three original probe inputs as assertions and a 512-deep document parsed via Task.detached; the temporary AUDITDiagnosticsTests.swift probes were deleted in the same commit. No byte cap added: the measured inputs are 25 KB and 100 KB, so size does not bound depth.
tasks.evidence_after: swift test --sanitize=address --filter 'MarkupDepthTests|ProviderContractTests|HTMLExtractorTests' => 81 tests, 0 failures, exit 0 (the run that previously ended in AddressSanitizer: BUS), including a 512-deep document parsed on a cooperative task. swift test --filter 'MarkupDepthTests|HTMLExtractorTests|FetchFallbackTests|FetchBehaviorTests' => 45 tests, 0 failures. Full suite swift test => 390 tests, 6 skipped, 0 failures (baseline 371/6, so +19 regression tests). swift build and swift build -c release => 0 warnings, 0 errors (baseline 0). Artifact: AUDIT/evidence/A01-asan.txt. Removing either the depth guard or the large-stack hop makes MarkupDepthTests kill the runner again (SIGBUS / signal 4).
tasks.notes: Reachability: web_open parses arbitrary attacker-controlled pages; the scraper path is opt-in but enabled in some deployments. Depth 5000 is ~25 KB of markup, 20000 is ~100 KB, both far below the 4 MiB response cap, so size limits do not bound depth; body size is capped where bodies are read. Item (3) of the fix was promoted from belt-and-braces to load-bearing by measurement: with the depth cap alone, a document AT the cap still overflowed a cooperative task stack under AddressSanitizer. Rather than lower the cap until the instrument was satisfied (which would make a production parameter depend on a debug build), the parse got a stack with room for the bound.

tasks.title: Executable coverage is unmeasured: the MCP surface reports 0 % because tests drive it as a subprocess, and the monitor reports 29.5 %
tasks.discovered_by: audit baseline: llvm-cov export over the test bundle
tasks.evidence_before: repo Sources/ = 84.3 % lines overall, WebSearchCore 88.2 %, SwiftWebSearchMCP 0 measured lines/functions, MCPSMonitor 29.5 %. Evidence: AUDIT/baseline/coverage-sources.txt
tasks.notes: The MCP surface is behaviourally covered by StdioServerTests, HTTPTransportTests and mcp_smoke.py, but a metric of 0 % means the most contract-critical code is invisible to any coverage gate. Plan: make the subprocess emit coverage (LLVM_PROFILE_FILE in the child, merge profdata) or add in-process tests where the transport allows; add a coverage floor for Sources/ only.

tasks.title: Environment-variable contracts between units have no automated consistency check
tasks.evidence_before: AppConfiguration.Key is the source of truth for the server; scripts, compose, the provisioning script and CI set the same names as strings with no compile-time or test-time link; a rename breaks a consumer silently
tasks.notes: Plan: a test that asserts every variable in AppConfiguration.Key appears in example.env and that every SEARCH_*/*_API_KEY literal used by scripts and deploy exists as a Key, so drift fails the suite.
